definitions.gloss: to be visible, to be seen
definitions.explanation: For something to be perceivable by sight. The spontaneous/potential form of seeing.

definitions.gloss: to appear, to look, to seem
definitions.explanation: To give a certain impression or appearance.
Polite form meaning 'to come' or 'to visit,' used for respected persons.

examples.japanese: ここから{富士山|ふじさん}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: You can see Mt. Fuji from here.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{若|わか}く{見|み}える。
{先生|せんせい}がお{見|み}えになりました。
{遠|とお}くに{山|やま}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: I can see mountains in the distance.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さくて{見|み}えないから、もっと{大|おお}きく{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: I can't see it because it's too small, so please write it bigger.

examples.japanese: {星|ほし}がよく{見|み}える{夜|よる}です。
examples.english: It's a night when you can see the stars well.

examples.japanese: {霧|きり}で{何|なに}も{見|み}えない。
examples.english: I can't see anything because of the fog.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{疲|つか}れているように{見|み}える。
{簡単|かんたん}そうに{見|み}えるけど、{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It looks easy, but it's difficult.

examples.japanese: {その服|そのふく}を{着|き}ると{太|ふと}って{見|み}える。
examples.english: You look heavier when you wear those clothes.

examples.japanese: {幸|しあわ}せそうに{見|み}えますね。
{社長|しゃちょう}がお{見|み}えです。
お{客様|きゃくさま}がお{見|み}えになっています。
{先生|せんせい}は{何時|なんじ}にお{見|み}えになりますか。
examples.english: What time will the teacher arrive?

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}がまもなくお{見|み}えになると{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I think the department manager will arrive soon.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xが{見|み}える (X is visible) / Xに{見|み}える (appear as X, look like X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing state. {見|み}えている = 'is visible.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・Xが{見|み}える (X is visible)
・{若|わか}く{見|み}える (look young)
・〜に{見|み}える (look like ~, appear to be ~)
・お{見|み}えになる (come—honorific)
・{見|み}えない (can't see, invisible)

CONTRAST WITH {見|み}る:
・{見|み}る: active seeing/looking (transitive)
・{見|み}える: spontaneous/potential visibility (intransitive)

PARALLEL: {聞|き}く → {聞|き}こえる follows the same pattern (hear → be audible).
